# Scaled picture shadows

Original controls generated by `tools/scaled_picture_shadows_fixture.py` from
the project's original picture-shadow texture/OPC package. No template art or
third-party font binaries are included. The reference application exported the
retained PDF after verifying the exact source path.

Fourteen pages cover nine alignment anchors with unequal 150%/50% scales,
150% scale with 6pt blur, negative horizontal/vertical scales, a zero horizontal
scale, and 102% scale with 36pt blur. Source frames stay 144pt square at
(72pt,100pt); shadows do not change those layout frames. The page was enlarged
to 432pt square so the expanded effects remain visible.

ECMA-376 Part 1 fifth edition §20.1.8.45 (PDF pages 2883–2884, zero-based)
specifies alignment before scale/skew/offset and negative scale as a flip.
The schema defaults alignment to bottom-center and scale to 100%. No native
contradiction was found for the supported scaling behavior. Nonzero skew,
rotated frames and previously unsupported effect combinations remain guarded.

`tools/scaled_picture_shadows_reference.py` records source/PDF hashes and 17,408
native RGB samples. The first thirteen controls match within four RGB levels.
For blurred samples, the existing shadow-oracle allowance is retained: one
native shadow texel plus half a CSS pixel of sampling position. Editing tests
retain all fourteen pages, preserve unrelated package parts and original
shadow XML, undo exactly, and reopen editable. Unit checks cover percentage
spellings, the default alignment, signed/zero scales and resource rejection.

## Known large-blur PDF-export gap

The 36pt-blur control does not meet the PDF-export color tolerance, even with the
native-texel allowance. native reference PDF export uses a 47-by-47 shadow image over a 216.79pt square.
Before the wide-blur density correction, at (224pt,140pt), native RGB was
(221,204,237) and the scaled preview was (214,193,234). A private unscaled copy
also differed: the same native
color versus preview (217,198,236). Thus large-blur fidelity remains an issue
independent of accepting scale declarations. The Gaussian approximation and
the reference application's coarse shadow rasterization are not claimed equivalent.

An explicit expected-failure browser test retains the PDF-export requirement;
it must become an ordinary passing test when that defect is fixed. The passing
scaling test does not count this case as native-equivalent. The original shoe
flyer is now editable with its image present, but remains a partial review.

The later [opaque square controls](../shadow-blur-profile/README.md) isolated
excess center density without texture transparency or scaling. The wide-blur
Gaussian calculation now passes all twelve square profiles, including the
previously failing 72pt square with 48pt blur. This textured control still has
nine samples outside tolerance, each by one RGB level. Its expected failure
remains until the remaining raster-sampling discrepancy is resolved.

## Native metafile comparison (2026-09-28)

`metafile/` retains the same page-14 range from the reference application as an EMF,
its Windows GDI+ playback, and extracted original image objects. This native
path uses a 140-by-140 shadow bitmap; PDF export uses 47-by-47. It is not a
screen capture and does not establish exact on-screen native pixel identity.

The original range viewport clips the bottom of the shadow. The capture tool
expands only the EMF header's rclFrame bottom and scales the destination height
by the identical ratio. The recorder verifies byte equality everywhere else,
pixel equality throughout the original viewport, and that native drawing
bounds fit inside the expanded image. Header bounds, not the .NET logical
viewport bounds, determine the expansion. A floating-point destination rectangle
avoids rounding the playback scale. The unmodified EMF and PNG remain available.

The physical picture anchor and extent come from the source OOXML. Its native
transform maps the existing 1,223 sample positions into the GDI+ image. The
unchanged allowance (one shadow texel plus 0.375pt) becomes 17 native pixels.
All positions are tested, including white background outside the image; none
are excluded. The ordinary browser regression allows the existing four RGB
levels. The PDF-export expected failure remains separate and unchanged in
scope. This evidence does not justify modifying the production blur kernel or
color channels to match PDF-only differences. Corpus #128 remains partial.

Reproduce with `tools/capture-wide-shadow-metafile.ps1` (reference application and
Windows GDI+), then `tools/record_wide_shadow_metafile.py` (Pillow). Use
`-RenderExisting` to replay the retained native EMF without opening the reference application.
All embedded picture assets and source controls were authored in this project;
no third-party fonts, template artwork or rendering engine are redistributed.
